attributes.name: Agility
attributes.description: Governs physical finesse, dexterity, and nimbleness. It's how you avoid getting hit in melee combat, take to feats of acrobatics, swing your sword, or fire your gun.

attributes.name: Brawn
attributes.description: Governs physical force, strength, and might. It's how hard you can hit, how much you can lift, how long you can run or hold your breath, and how imposing you can be with your physicality.

attributes.name: Knowledge
attributes.description: Governs learning, intellect, and mental skillsets. It's how you learn languages, recall scientific or historical information, train to use medicine, or display educational prowess.

attributes.name: Perception
attributes.description: Governs tasks and skills related to awareness, insight, and situations. It's how you know where to place your foot while sneaking, locate clues from a scene, or ride your horse while avoiding obstacles.

skills.name: Acrobatics
skills.description: Feats of dexterous physicality: climbing a wall or rope, jumping over obstacles, balancing on a ledge, and similar precision physical work. Climb, jump, or tightrope-walk meters equal to your die code.
skills.time: one round (longer climbs take multiple rounds)

skills.name: Melee
skills.description: Hand-to-hand combat: brawling with fists, improvised weapons, and the use of swords, axes, and more. Melee attacks are rolled against the target's Parry.

skills.name: Shooting
skills.description: Use of ranged weapons that are not thrown, such as bows, firearms, and crossbows. Attacks are rolled against the target's Dodge.

skills.name: Sleight of Hand
skills.description: Nimbleness of fingers: picking a pocket, hiding small objects, picking a lock, or precise hand movements such as unlocking a puzzle box.
skills.time: one round (some tasks take a few more)

skills.name: Athletics
skills.description: Raw physical strength, endurance, and stamina: lifting, pushing, restraining, or strength-based activities such as swimming. A character can generally lift 100 lbs. per die code with a successful Difficulty 10 roll.
skills.time: one round (some tasks take a few more)

skills.name: Intimidation
skills.description: Using your physical mass, might, and appearance to cause fear in others: looming over a foe, flexing, or breaking something to show your strength.

skills.name: Stamina
skills.description: Holding your breath, running long distances, dealing with force marches, and resisting poison, pain, or disease. A character can hold their breath roughly a minute per rank of Stamina.
skills.time: usually a response, not an action

skills.name: Throwing
skills.description: How far a character can hurl an item, be it an axe, a ball, letters, or a bag of loot. A character can throw an item roughly 1 meter per die code when it is 15 kilograms or less.

skills.name: Languages
skills.description: Deciphering obscure dialects, learning new languages, and dealing with the intricacies of tongues. A character always knows their native language; each point grants a conversational talent in a new language or dialect.

skills.name: Medicine
skills.description: Diagnosing diseases, healing the hurt, and creating poultices and salves. Can remove damage: Difficulty 10 for stunned, 15 for wounded or incapacitated, 20 for mortally wounded.

skills.name: Scholar
skills.description: Academic pursuits outside the sciences: art, history, philosophy, religion, and other 'humanities' fields of study.

skills.name: Sciences
skills.description: Scientific pursuits such as biology, chemistry, geology, astronomy, and engineering, plus technology and the study of natural life and fauna.

skills.name: Driving
skills.description: A broad transportation skill covering riding a horse, driving a car or carriage, and piloting a boat or craft.

skills.name: Investigation
skills.description: Gathering information, researching, analyzing data, or creating a pattern from data, based on identifying the valuable and essential information.
skills.time: an action (larger scenes may take longer)

skills.name: Stealth
skills.description: Remaining unnoticed: knowing where to step, reading the patterns of guards, and finding good hiding spaces. Opposed by Investigation.

skills.name: Survival
skills.description: Finding your way in the wilderness, calming or managing animals, knowing what foods are poisonous or healthy, treating injured animals, and tending crops.

woundLevels.name: Staggered
woundLevels.text: -1D penalty on all die codes rolled (not Brawn rolls to resist damage). Goes away at the start of the next round. Being staggered again while staggered makes you stunned instead.

woundLevels.name: Stunned
woundLevels.text: Can't do anything for the rest of the combat round. Goes away at the start of the next round. A Hero Point can be spent to avoid being stunned.

woundLevels.name: Wounded
woundLevels.text: Fall prone and can't do anything for the rest of this round. All skill and attribute checks are reduced by 1D (not Brawn rolls to resist damage). Goes away after medical treatment or 24 hours' rest. A wounded character wounded again is incapacitated.

woundLevels.name: Incapacitated
woundLevels.text: Fall prone and unconscious; can't do anything until healed. Goes away after 24 hours or medical treatment. An incapacitated character wounded again is mortally wounded.

woundLevels.name: Mortally Wounded
woundLevels.text: Fall prone and unconscious; can't do anything until healed. At the end of every combat round, roll 2D; if the total is less than the number of rounds since being mortally wounded, the character dies. Only goes away after medical treatment.

damageResults.range: Brawn Roll greater than Damage Roll
Brawn Roll equal to or less than Damage Roll
Brawn Roll equal to or less than Damage Roll, and Damage Roll invoked a Complication

combatModifiers.name: Preparing
combatModifiers.text: Spend a round doing nothing to aim/prepare: +1D to the skill roll next round (only when using a single skill).

combatModifiers.name: Running
combatModifiers.text: -1D to any skill rolls made in a round the character runs.

combatModifiers.name: Wounded
combatModifiers.text: -1D to skill and attribute checks while wounded.

combatModifiers.name: Staggered
combatModifiers.text: -1D to all die codes rolled while staggered.

combatModifiers.name: Extra action segment
combatModifiers.text: Each action segment after the first applies -1D to any die codes used during that combat round (multiple skill uses stack).

combatModifiers.name: Prone vs. melee
combatModifiers.text: A prone character has a maximum Dodge and Parry of 10 against melee attacks.

combatModifiers.name: Prone vs. ranged
combatModifiers.text: A prone character adds +10 to their Dodge score against ranged attacks.

combatModifiers.name: Crawling
combatModifiers.text: A crawling (prone) character's die code is reduced by 1D, like a running character.

creation.note: Add +3D attribute dice for each additional attribute over four; add +2D skill dice per optional skill module the GM uses. Dice are assigned one-for-one; each attribute must be at least 1D and no higher than 5D at creation.

heroPoints.name: Double a roll
heroPoints.text: Spend 1 Hero Point to double the Die Code of a single roll.

heroPoints.name: Reroll
heroPoints.text: Spend 1 Hero Point to reroll a failed roll without doubling down.

heroPoints.name: Avoid being stunned
heroPoints.text: Spend 1 Hero Point to avoid being stunned in combat.

quickRules.title: The Wild Die
quickRules.text: One die in every code is the Wild Die (a different color/size). A 6 grants an Advantage; a 1 causes a Complication. You must always include the Wild Die.

quickRules.title: Doubling Down
quickRules.text: After a failed non-combat action, narrate a retry and reroll the entire die code. Failing the retry gives a Complication but no Hero Point.

quickRules.title: Opposed Rolls
quickRules.text: Both sides roll the same attribute/skill; the higher score wins. On a tie, a PC beats an NPC; between PCs the highest Wild Die wins.

quickRules.title: Difficulty Numbers
quickRules.text: The GM sets a Difficulty Number; a score greater than the DN succeeds. Equal or lower fails.

quickRules.title: Preparing
quickRules.text: Do nothing for one round to gain +1D on next round's roll. Only works when you use a single skill that round.

quickRules.title: Running
quickRules.text: A character who runs in a combat round has all skill rolls reduced by 1D that round. Walking moves 5m, running 10m.

quickRules.title: Wounds
quickRules.text: A wounded character rolls skills and attributes at -1D (never affects Brawn rolls to resist damage).

quickRules.title: Multiple Actions
quickRules.text: You may use more than one skill in a round; every action segment after the first applies -1D to all die codes used that round.

quickRules.title: Cancelling Modifiers
quickRules.text: Increases and reductions add together; e.g. a wounded character preparing (+1D) cancels the wound's -1D and uses the unmodified code.

quickRules.title: Defenses
quickRules.text: Dodge (5 x Perception dice) resists ranged attacks, surprises, and traps; Parry (5 x Agility dice) blocks melee attacks.

quickRules.title: Damage
quickRules.text: On a hit, roll weapon damage; the target rolls Brawn (plus armor). Brawn beats damage = staggered; Brawn equal/less = wounded; equal/less with a damage Complication = mortally wounded.

quickRules.title: Prone
quickRules.text: Fall prone at the end of movement with no penalty. Prone characters crawl up to 2m/round at -1D, are harder to hit, and can drop prone when struck.
